facts.text: Turning the wheel of time (Yugparavartan) indicates a change of an age, the emergence of a new set of thoughts and social values.
facts.quote: Turning the wheel of time (Yugparavartan) indicates a change of an age, the emergence of a new set of thoughts and social values.

facts.text: In the 4th century BCE, a new age began with the establishment of the Mauryan Empire; Chandragupta was helped by Arya Chanakya.
facts.quote: In the 4th century BCE, a new age began with the establishment of the Mauryan Empire. ... He was helped in this task by Arya Chanakya.

facts.text: King Dhananand of the Nanda dynasty ruled the Magadha Empire; he was immensely wealthy and people were unhappy about his rule.
facts.quote: King Dhananand of the Nanda dynasty was ruling over the Magadha Empire. He was immensely wealthy. People were unhappy about his rule.

facts.text: Chandragupta established the Maurya empire by defeating Dhananand in 321 BCE.
facts.quote: King Chandragupta established Maurya empire by defeating Dhananand in 321 BCE.

facts.text: Later Chandragupta conquered Avanti and Saurashtra and expanded the Maurya empire.
facts.quote: Later he conquered Avanti and Saurashtra and expanded Maurya empire.

facts.text: Chanakya is also known as Kautilya or Vishnugupta; he was a great statesman and scholar.
facts.quote: Chanakya is also known as 'Kautilya' or 'Vishnugupta'. He was a great statesman and scholar.

facts.text: Chanakya wrote the Arthashastra, which deals with governance, tax system, defence, intelligence and politics.
facts.quote: Chanakya authored a treatise titled 'Arthashastra'. It deals with subject like governance, tax system, defence, Intelligence and politics.

facts.text: As a child, Chandragupta played the role of a king and held his 'court' under a tree; Chanakya noticed his leadership qualities.
facts.quote: Chandragupta as a child, while playing with his friends used to enact the role of a king. He used to hold his 'court' under a tree. ... He noticed Chandragupta's inherent leadership qualities

facts.text: Chanakya trained Chandragupta in warfare and administration.
facts.quote: Then, Chanakya took Chandragupta with him. Trained him in warfare and administration.

facts.text: The Sanskrit play Mudrarakshasa, written by Vishakhadatta, tells how Chandragupta Maurya came to power by defeating Dhananand.
facts.quote: The Sanskrit play 'Mudrarakshasa', written by Vishakhadatta, gives an account of Chandragupta Maurya coming to power, by defeating Dhananand.

facts.text: The Greek Emperor Alexander (Sikandar) invaded the northwestern region of the Indian subcontinent in 326 BCE and reached up to the Punjab province.
facts.quote: The Greek Emperor Alexander (Sikandar) invaded the northwestern region of the Indian subcontinent in 326 BCE. He had reached up to the Punjab province in India.

facts.text: Alexander appointed governors called Satrapa to administer the conquered territories; after his death they fought for power.
facts.quote: He had appointed governors to administer the territories he had conquered. These governors were known as 'Satrapa'. After his death, conflict began among these Satrapas for power.

facts.text: The Greek General Seleucus Nicator attempted to invade India and was defeated by Chandragupta Maurya.
facts.quote: the Greek General Seleucus Nicator attempted to invade India. He was defeated by Chandragupta Maurya.

facts.text: The provinces of Kabul, Kandahar and Herat in Afghanistan were incorporated into Chandragupta Maurya's empire.
facts.quote: The provinces of Kabul, Kandahar and Herat in Afganistan were incorporated into Chandragupta Maurya's empire.

facts.text: Megasthenes, the ambassador of Seleucus Nicator, was appointed in Chandragupta Maurya's court; his book Indica is an important source of Mauryan history.
facts.quote: Megasthenes, the ambassador of Seleucus Nicator, was appointed in Chandragupta Maurya's court. The descriptions in 'Indica', a book written by him serves as an important source of Indian history during the Mauryan period.

facts.text: During Chandragupta Maurya's time, the Sudarshan lake was built at Junagadh (present-day Gujarat) for agriculture, irrigation and drinking water; special caretakers looked after it.
facts.quote: During Chandragupta Maurya's time, a lake named 'Sudarshan' was constructed at Junagadh, located in the present-day state of Gujarat. This lake was useful to facilitate agriculture, irrigation and the supply of drinking water. Special caretakers were oppointed

facts.text: The Arthashastra contains details about penalties for a person causing damage to a water reservoir.
facts.quote: The 'Arthashastra' contains details about the penalties to be imposed on a person causing damage to a water reservoir.

facts.text: Emperor Ashoka, the Shaka King Rudradaman and later rulers repaired the Sudarshan Lake; this is recorded in Rudradaman's Junagadh inscription.
facts.quote: Emperor Ashoka, the Shaka King Rudradaman and rulers of later periods repaired the Sudarshan Lake. The references to these efforts are found in the Rudradaman's Junagadh inscription.

facts.text: Towards the end of his rule, Chandragupta gave up his kingship, accepted Jainism and lived at Shravanabelagola in Karnataka.
facts.quote: Towards the end of his rule, Chandragupta gave up his kingship and accepted Jainism. He lived at Shravanabelagola in Karnataka.

facts.text: Chandragupta's son Bindusara continued the expansion and made friendly relations with the Indo-Greek Satrapas; the empire's political and economic foundation grew stronger.
facts.quote: After Chandragupta, his son Bindusara came to power. Bindusara continued the expansion of the kingdom. He established friendly relations with the Indo-Greek Satrapas. During his rule, the political and economic foundation of the Maurya Empire further strengthened.

facts.text: After Bindusara's death, his son Ashoka became the king.
facts.quote: After Bindusara's death, his son Ashoka became the king.

facts.text: Bindusara had appointed Ashoka as the Governor of Ujjayini (Ujjain) and Takshashila.
facts.quote: Bindusara had appointed Ashoka as the Governor of Ujjayini (Ujjain) and Takshashila.

facts.text: Ashoka's empire extended from Afghanistan in the northwest and Nepal in the north to Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh in the south, and from Bengal in the east to Saurashtra in the west.
facts.quote: Emperor Ashoka's empire extended from Afghanistan in the northwest and Nepal in the north to Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh in the south, as well as from Bengal in the east to Saurashtra in the west.

facts.text: The most important event in Ashoka's life was the Kalinga War; Kalinga, in present-day Odisha, was not part of the Mauryan Empire, so Ashoka invaded it and won.
facts.quote: The most important event in Emperor Ashoka's life was the Kalinga War. The ancient kingdom of Kalinga was situated within present-day state of Odisha. Kalinga was not a part of the Mauryan Empire. Therefore, Ashoka invaded Kalinga. He won this war.

facts.text: Many soldiers were killed in the Kalinga War; Ashoka was filled with grief and the war completely transformed him.
facts.quote: In this war, large number of soldiers were killed and many were imprisoned. Ashoka was filled with grief ... This war completely transformed Emperor Ashoka.

facts.text: Ashoka embraced Buddhism and gave special importance to non-violence, caring for parents and respect for teachers and elders.
facts.quote: Ashoka embraced Buddhism. He gave special importance to the principles like non-violence, caring for one's parents, and respect for teachers and elders.

facts.text: Ashoka used rock and pillar inscriptions to spread his message; most are engraved in Brahmi script.
facts.quote: Emperor Ashoka made use of rock and pillar inscriptions to spread his message. Most of these inscriptions are engraved in Brahmi script.

facts.text: In his inscriptions Ashoka calls himself 'Devanam Piyo Piyadasi', meaning 'Beloved of the Gods and he who looks on with affection'.
facts.quote: he refers to himself as 'Devanam Piyo Piyadasi'. The meaning of this is 'Beloved of the Gods and he who looks on with affection'.

facts.text: Ashoka appointed officials dedicated to the Dhamma, called Dhamma-Mahamattas, who conveyed the message of morality to the people.
facts.quote: These officials were known as 'Dhamma-Mahamattas'. These officials used to convey the message of morality to the people.

facts.text: Ashoka sent his son Mahendra and his daughter Sanghamitra to Sri Lanka to spread Dharma.
facts.quote: he sent his son Mahendra and his daughter Sanghamitra, to Sri Lanka to spread Dharma.

facts.text: Ashoka sent messengers west to Syria, Egypt and Greece, and east to Myanmar.
facts.quote: Ashoka dispatched messengers to distant places to the west, including Syria, Egypt and Greece, and Myanmar to the east.

facts.text: Ashoka held a Buddhist Council at Pataliputra.
facts.quote: Ashoka also held a Buddhist Council at Pataliputra.

facts.text: Ashoka established hospitals, dispensaries and rest houses, planted trees along roads, provided wells and drinking water stands, and built veterinary clinics.
facts.quote: He established hospitals, dispensaries and rest houses. He planted trees on both sides of the roads ... He also made provisions for wells and public drinking water stands. He constructed veterinary clinics.

facts.text: Heads of departments were called Adhyakshas, e.g. Panyadhyaksha (Chief Officer of Trade) and Sitadhyaksha (Chief Officer of Agriculture).
facts.quote: These heads were referred to as 'Adhyakshas' (Superintendents) of the respective departments. For example; 'Panyadhyaksha' (Chief Officer of Trade) and 'Sitadhyaksha' (Chief Officer of Agriculture).

facts.text: During the Mauryan period, the intelligence department was extremely powerful; the Arthashastra describes the spy system in detail.
facts.quote: During the Mauryan period, the intelligence department was extremely powerful. Kautilya's Arthashastra contains a detailed description of the spy system.

facts.text: The kingdom was divided into four provinces with capitals: East - Toshali, West - Ujjayini, North - Takshashila, South - Suvarnagiri.
facts.quote: the kingdom was divided into four provinces. Region Capital East Toshali West Ujjayini North Takshashila South Suvarnagiri

facts.text: All decisions regarding the empire were made in the capital, Pataliputra.
facts.quote: All decisions regarding the empire were made in the capital, Pataliputra.

facts.text: In provincial administration, each region was governed with the help of a Kumar (Prince) and a Mahamatya (Chief Administrative Officer).
facts.quote: Each region was governed with the assistance of a Kumar (Prince) and a Mahamatya (Chief Administrative Officer).

facts.text: In local administration, daily affairs like taxation, justice and law and order were managed by Gramanis (village head) in villages and by local committees in cities.
facts.quote: daily affairs including taxation, justice and law and order were managed by Gramanis (Village head), and in the cities by local committees.

facts.text: Sculptures of the Maurya period featured animals such as lions, elephants and bulls; the style is realistic.
facts.quote: Sculptures of Maurya period featured animals such as lions, elephants and bulls. The sculptural style is realistic.

facts.text: The Barabar Caves in Bihar are the most ancient rock-cut caves in India.
facts.quote: The Barabar Caves in Bihar of this period are the most ancient rock-cut caves in India.

facts.text: The Sanchi Stupa and the Sarnath Stupa are excellent examples of Mauryan architecture.
facts.quote: The Sanchi Stupa and the Sarnath Stupa are excellent examples of the architecture of this period.

facts.text: During the Maurya period, rock surfaces were polished to a mirror-like finish.
facts.quote: During the Maurya period, rock surfaces were polished to attain a mirror-like finish.

facts.text: Foreign travellers described the beautiful royal palace at Pataliputra.
facts.quote: The travelogues written by various foreign travellers to India, contain descriptions of the beautiful royal palace at Pataliputra.

facts.text: The daily diet included milk, curd, ghee, various fruits, rice and barley.
facts.quote: the daily diet included items such as milk, curd, clarified butter (ghee), various fruits, rice and barley.

facts.text: Megasthenes wrote that people were hardworking and frugal, farmers harvested two crops a year, enemies did not destroy crops, theft happened rarely and slavery did not exist.
facts.quote: the people here are hardworking and frugal. ... Farmers harvest two crops a year. ... Even enemies do not destroy the crops. ... Theft happens rarely. ... Slavery did not exist

facts.text: After Ashoka, the Maurya Empire weakened; Pushyamitra Shunga established the Shunga dynasty by defeating Brihadratha, the last king of the Maurya Empire.
facts.quote: After Emperor Ashoka, the power of the Maurya Empire gradually began to diminish. ... Pushyamitra Shunga established the Shunga dynasty by defeating Brihadratha the last king of the Maurya Empire.
